tagline: From Idaho's oldest building down to a white pine mill town.
intro: From the interstate near Rose Lake, Idaho 3 follows and crosses the Coeur d'Alene River and turns south through marshland spotted with the lakes the river feeds, past Medimont on the north shore of Cave Lake. It crosses the St. Joe into St. Maries. From there Idaho 6 runs southwest past Emida and the Hoodoo Mountains to Harvard on the Palouse River, and ends at Potlatch.
St. Maries began with a sawmill in 1889, set just southwest of the meeting of the St. Maries and St. Joe rivers, which floated the logs to the mill and carried the steamboats away with the lumber.

moments.title: Old Mission State Park
moments.text: Father Antonio Ravalli had the Mission of the Sacred Heart built of wattle and daub without a single nail, and it stands today as the oldest building in Idaho.

moments.title: Harvard
moments.text: Homer Canfield declined to have the railroad stop named for him and suggested Harvard instead, to keep company with Princeton five miles west.

moments.title: Potlatch
moments.text: Weyerhaeuser's company built the largest white pine sawmill in the world here, and a town around it where only married couples could rent the houses.
